structured_output.summary: The loop has one solid result. E005 (Lookahead/EMA) is the first run to meet the bar: +0.97 pp, and every seed gained 0.85–1.15 pp. The bookkeeping around it is unreliable, though. (1) E005's description says 9 epochs, but its time (+0.6% vs E004) and the post-mortem ("10-epoch run") show it ran at 10 epochs on the E004 base. As a result, H1.3.2's "at 9 epochs fixed" premise is unmet, and the plan to spend the 0.53 pp margin by trimming epochs starts from the wrong number. (2) E002 tested 9→10 epochs, but its "supports" verdict went to H4.2.1, which predicts 8.5→9. Most of that +0.66 pp gain comes from E001's single 0.7355 seed-1 outlier; with that seed excluded the gain is about 0.28 pp. That slope then feeds the "EMA ≈ 1.5 epochs" claim and the epoch-trim plan. (3) The tree's status and confidence columns were never updated: H1.1.1 is still open after its pre-registered refutation, E004 is not attached to H2.2.1, and the E003 recompile leak is not filed as evidence for H3.1. (4) Measured prepare times (0.06–0.21 s, about 1–2% of 9 s) already contradict H3.2 and most of H3. (5) Compiled training is deterministic per seed, so re-running a recipe measures no accuracy noise. The only noise estimate available is that compiling without changing the math moved per-seed accuracy by up to 0.35 pp. Mean differences under about 0.3 pp should therefore be treated as noise. (6) The E005 jump is explained by end-of-run variance reduction, but that is untested. Lookahead's effect on the training trajectory, or a final LR that stays too high (0.07 of peak), would explain it equally well. No hypothesis covers the CIFAR-10-tuned hyperparameters (lr 9.0, wd 0.012, widths, the floor of the LR schedule) carried over unchanged to CIFAR-100. Muon, label smoothing, flip, whitening, progressive resizing and CUDA graphs are all untested.

critiques.issue: The description says 'at 9 epochs', but the time (9.10 s, +0.6% vs the 10-epoch E004) and the post-mortem ('in a 10-epoch run') show E005 ran at 10 epochs. Either the run was 10 epochs, so H1.3.2's 'at 9 epochs fixed' premise is not what was tested, or it was 9 epochs and the time comparison is wrong. The next step ('trim epochs to spend the 0.53 pp margin') depends on which epoch count the margin belongs to.
critiques.suggestion: Read the epoch count from the E005 commit, fix the description, and record E005 as evidence for an un-pinned version of H1.3.2 (EMA at the base recipe's epoch count). Start every epoch-trim experiment from the verified E005 epoch count.

critiques.issue: H4.2.1 predicts the change from 8.5 to 9 epochs (+0.2–0.5 pp, +4–8% time). E002 ran 9→10 epochs and was judged against a different rule (0.4–1.2 pp, +9–13%) written in the notebook. The '+' was recorded for a prediction that was never tested. The +0.66 pp is also a single pair, and most of it is E001's seed-1 outlier (0.7355). With that seed excluded, 9→10 epochs gains only about 0.28 pp.
critiques.suggestion: Change E002's token on H4.2.1 to ~ (inconclusive), or move it to H4.2 as weak evidence. Measure the slope where it will be used: E005-recipe at N vs N−0.5 epochs, with EMA, since EMA likely flattens the accuracy-vs-epoch curve.

critiques.issue: This conversion uses the 0.66 pp/epoch slope from the noisy no-EMA E002 pair. It also assumes EMA's gain and extra epochs are interchangeable, which is untested: EMA may give less benefit at lower epoch counts, or more.
critiques.suggestion: Treat the conversion as unknown. Measure EMA's gain at a second epoch count (e.g. 9) before relying on it to plan cuts.

critiques.issue: The post-mortem credits the gain to end-of-run averaging removing weight noise. Two other explanations fit equally well: (a) Lookahead (resetting fast weights to slow weights every 5 steps) changes the whole training trajectory, not just the endpoint; (b) the triangular schedule stops at 0.07 of peak LR, so any noise reduction would help, e.g. annealing to 0. It is also unstated whether BN running stats come from the EMA or the raw weights.
critiques.suggestion: Add Lvl3 tests: (i) final LR → 0 without EMA; (ii) EMA of weights only, applied at the end, without Lookahead resets; (iii) E005 plus final LR → 0. If (i) matches E005, EMA's ~0.6% time cost is avoidable. Also confirm the BN buffers come from the EMA weights.

critiques.issue: E001 refuted it by the pre-registered rule (0.7430 < 0.745), yet it is still 'open' at confidence 0.60.
critiques.suggestion: Set status to refuted and lower its confidence; the time half held, but the prediction is a conjunction.

critiques.issue: Only E003~ is recorded. E004 (the bug-fixed re-run) gave −14% steady-state time with the same accuracy, which matches the prediction, but nothing was attached to H2.2.1. H2's 10–25% claim also now has a confirming data point, and confidences are unchanged.
critiques.suggestion: Add E004+ to H2.2.1 and raise the confidence of H2.2/H2. Note that the 14% is a bundle (compile + fused SGD + channels_last), so no single component has been isolated.

critiques.issue: E003 showed exactly the mechanism H3.1 describes: a stride-guard recompile leaking about 9 s into the timed region. It is not recorded as evidence there.
critiques.suggestion: Attach E003+ to H3.1, and make 'TORCH_LOGS=recompiles on random data' a required pre-launch check for any change to the compiled graph (new resolution, EMA swap, batch size).

critiques.issue: Measured prepare time is 0.06–0.21 s, about 0.7–2.3% of a 9 s trial, and E000's whole fixed overhead is 0.14 s. That already contradicts H3.2 (prepare ≥ 5%) and makes H3.2.1's '30% prepare cut' worth about 0.03 s. H3's '>10% fixed cost' is only plausible if some cost hides inside train(), and that was never measured.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H3.2 refuted by E001/E004 and prune H3.2.1. Keep H3 only if a profile of the first train step against steady state shows a hidden one-time cost. The one visible effect is trial 0's prepare (0.21 vs 0.06 s), which is worth about 0.05 s on the mean and should be checked once.

critiques.issue: E003 and E004 produced bit-identical accuracy, so re-running a recipe measures no accuracy noise, and the 3 fixed seeds will be over-fit by every kept change. Within-run per-seed std ranged from about 0.13 pp (E002) to 0.65 pp (E001). The only estimate of trajectory noise is that compiling without changing the math moved per-seed accuracy by up to 0.35 pp (E002 → E003), so 3-seed mean differences under about 0.3 pp are not resolvable. The note that E001's seed-1 drop was 'not a seed property' is not established: E002 changed the schedule, so its seed-1 trajectory was a different run.
critiques.suggestion: Rewrite H4.1.1: the accuracy part can't be tested by re-running. If the harness allows offline runs, run the current best recipe on extra seeds (e.g. 3–12) once, to estimate the 40-seed mean against the 3-seed mean and the real per-seed std. Require a gain of ≥ 0.3 pp in the mean before crediting any accuracy change.

critiques.issue: The plan aims to sit just above 0.753 on seeds 0–2. Nothing checks whether seeds 0–2 run above or below the population mean; E001's seed 1 shows a single seed can drop 1 pp.
critiques.suggestion: Before the final epoch trim, check the chosen recipe on held-out seeds offline and keep about 0.3 pp of margin over 0.75 on the 40-seed estimate.

critiques.target: Missing Lvl2 under H1: hyperparameter transfer
critiques.issue: lr 9.0, wd 0.012, widths 128/384/576, batch size 1024 and the 0.07 LR floor were all copied from CIFAR-10 airbench settings. No hypothesis covers whether they suit CIFAR-100 short runs, even though E005 suggests the endpoint is far from settled.
critiques.suggestion: Add H1.5: 'CIFAR-10-tuned optimizer and schedule settings are off for CIFAR-100'. Give it Lvl3 tests for the final LR floor, a coarse lr×wd grid (×0.5/×2) and LS 0.2 vs 0.3 (H1.3.1, still untested), each at a fixed epoch count on the E005 base.

critiques.target: Untested directions (H1.2, H1.1.2, H1.4.1, H2.3, H2.2.2, H2.4)
critiques.issue: Muon, removing whitening/Dirac init, alternating vs random flip, progressive resizing, CUDA graphs and loss-based example selection have no experiments yet. H2.1.1 can no longer be tested in isolation, because the GPU data pipeline was bundled into E001.
critiques.suggestion: Prune H2.1.1. Order the rest by expected seconds saved: H2.3 (resolution, ~5%+), H1.2 (Muon, fewer epochs), H2.2.2 (CUDA graphs; first profile whether the ~18 ms steps are CPU-launch-bound under the 4-core pin). Leave H1.1.2/H1.4.1 for later: they are ablations that would only confirm the current choices and won't cut time.

critiques.issue: Judging runs on an A100 PCIe (lower power limit), while all timings here are on SXM4. The max-autotune kernel choices and the ~9 s figure may not carry over, especially for compute-bound kernels.
critiques.suggestion: Treat absolute times as SXM-specific and rank recipes on relative time. Avoid choices whose advantage depends on SXM's higher clocks.
